recipes.name: Pub-Style Vegetarian Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 tablespoon chili powder, or more to taste
1 (28 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes with juice
0.75 teaspoon hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook and stir mushrooms, onion, carrot, green bell pepper, celery, garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, black pepper, basil, and oregano in hot oil until onion begins to soften, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes with their liquid, black beans and their liquid, water, tomato paste, red wine, and hot pepper sauce.
Bring chili to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer until vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pub-Style Vegetarian Chili
raw_recipe.description: This vegetarian chili recipe is seasoned with flavorful spices, herbs, red wine, and hot sauce and features black beans and plenty of vegetables.

review.reviewBody: I used sliced Baby Bella mushrooms, chopped red bell peppers instead of green and I used what I call "a mess" of fresh garlic (and what I mean is instead of measuring out a tablespoon, I just chopped up a handful of fresh cloves). Instead of using water, I used organic beef broth. This is very, very good. I had a cup and a half for lunch today and I'm thinking about going back for more. What I love most about this is it's filling without going overboard and you can indulge and half a little more without feeling guilty. GREAT recipe--a snap to prepare.

Very good! Followed the recipe and didn't drain the beans, and used two cans of beans - one can red kidney beans and one can black beans - which was slightly more than 3 cups. Also used one 14 oz can of diced tomatoes and one 14 oz can of crushed to use up what I had on hand. Plus, I did everything in the Instant Pot® using the Sauté function for the first step, and the Bean/Chili function for the rest. That left a little more liquid than stove top, but we didn't care, it was so full of flavour. Great meatless recipe!

This recipe is a keeper for my collection. Very hearty and packed full of vegetables. A few adjustments I made and will keep are, I had fresh garlic on hand so I used 2 cloves and instead of whole peeled tomatoes, I used one can of diced tomatoes. As suggested by another user, I subbed the red wine for vegetable broth, and even added a little extra because I like a good amount of liquid. The recipe calls for sliced mushrooms, but next time I would cut them into smaller pieces. I will also start by sauteing the carrots first so they can get extra time before I throw in the rest of the vegetables because they certainly to firm. Can't wait to make this again!

Made this for NY day, and used 1 can black beans (drained!) and about a cup or so of black-eyed peas, to meet my southern tradition for New Year's. I think it's delicious, and very filling, but I found it to be too spicy, and I even cut down on some of the spices. I only used 1 tsp of cumin, not a tablespoon, and didn't have chili powder on hand so used a tsp. of paprika and tsp. of cayenne pepper instead. I only used a tsp. of salt, and one cup of water, because I like really chunky chili, not "soup" chili, plus the extra sodium is not needed! The consistency was perfect. Added a Tsp. of cocoa powder. Next time, I will just leave out the hot sauce to see if that fixes the slightly "too spicy" taste. I know some people really love spicy though! I also used red pepper, instead of green, as I don't care for green peppers. I garnished with some fresh sliced avocado and non-fat plain yogurt. Overall this is a great recipe and I will enjoy tweaking it.

This was delicious!
I made this recipe with what I had on hand, and I am sure it would have been just as good has I followed the recipe exactly. I used 1/2 the oil it called for; a yellow bell pepper instead of green; didn't add the red wine; two 14 oz. cans of diced tomatoes instead of the 28 oz. whole; added 1/2 tsp. of red pepper flakes instead of the hot sauce; added an extra 1/4 tsp. sea salt. I used two cans of black beans (drained and rinsed) and it was very close to 3 cups. Everything else was the same. It was a thinner chili, so I simmered it for 45 minutes to reduce the liquid. We dipped corn tortilla chips in it and it was fabulous!
Made a second time and we decided the celery is not needed. I would also like to try it without the tomato paste next time. I added some rice and ground beef and it was fabulous!

This is my new favorite veggie chili. I used all the ingredients listed. However, I used less olive oil, and cut the spices since I can't tolerate spicy foods. I did use the suggested amounts for oregano and basil and I used the full can of tomato paste. Instead of 3 cups of black beans, I used 2 cans of rinsed black beans and 1 can of rinsed northern beans. I like the addition of the white beans because it adds some color contrast to an otherwise dark and rather monochrome looking dish. I only buy diced canned tomatoes so that is what I used. The only change I will make next time is to at least double the mushrooms. I did make it the day before serving, as I usually do with chilis, so the flavors meld nicely. I am so happy I found this recipe! Delicious and nutritious!

I made this for a party and it’s was a hit. I added 1/3 cup of quinoa for protein and thickness, increased the chili powder and used a whole can of tomato paste, again to thicken. The mushrooms give it a nice texture, like a meat substitute. It’s good over rice. This will become a staple in my house!

This was a very good soup but too thin be what my husband considers chili. Still, we enjoyed it. I was worried about too much spice and heat and cut the chili powder and cumin by a teaspoon. I only used 1/8 tsp Tabasco. I also used a combination of orange and green pepper and beef broth for most of the water. Next time I won’t add any water.
Delicious staple in our house. We like to use broth instead of water, and we double the tomato paste. We also let it simmer for 40mins or longer to reduce liquid.

This is truly amazing!! You honestly do not miss or even realize there is no meat! Great as written but I used vegetable broth in place of water. No tomato paste. Added extra chili powder and cumin for my taste. Chopoed up one jalapeño. Used kidney, pinto and black beans. Also used red and green pepper. Threw everything in crockpot all at once.

My first time making a vegetarian chili as I am attempting to gradually cut meat out of my diet. It was delicious and I did not miss the meat. I did add a little can of tomato paste as the sauce seemed runny and I added 4 bay leaves as I always do to chili. Also added 1/2 cup of whole wheat berries as another review suggested and substituted coffee for the wine as I did not have wine. Not too spicy, I will add a bit more next time as I like it hot. And so filling!
This recipe was AMAZING!! We will definitely be making this again soon! I didn’t change anything.
Great flavour. I like a thicker chili so I just used less water. Loaded with veg, good source of protein.
Good flavors but way too thin. I won't add the water next time. Or double the rest of the ingredients and use the 2 cups of water; but then would the spices be off? This recipe needs some work.

This recipe was super easy to follow, and the result was delicious! I was worried the veggies wouldn't be soft enough, but they were just perfect. I had to make it without the garlic and I accidentally added twice as much tomato paste (whoops!) but it still came out great
Good as is, but I substitute cayenne for the hot sauce.
Amazing recipe. I used half the beans and added some vegan ground chik'n for texture, but it would also be great as is.
Excellent flavor! A lot more watery than chili, but didn't matter to me. I loved it. I used fresh herbs instead of dried.
Perfect consistency! Not too soupy... not too thick! It tasted great! I used sriracha in mine to give more of a kick! So good! Even my meat eating boyfriend loves it!

I made this for Halloween dinner. It turned out a little more like a hearty soup than chili but the flavor was outstanding. It was delicious. I used carrot straws instead of shredded carrot, so I think if I used shredded it would have been thicker.
